speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have experienced any difficulty swallowing or persistent coughing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That timeline of four weeks with significant weight loss is concerning. Do you have any fever, and have you noticed any lumps elsewhere on your body or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: A fixed, non-tender supraclavicular lymph node combined with significant weight loss and night sweats is highly concerning for malignancy, particularly lymphoma or metastatic disease. To help differentiate between these possibilities, have you noticed any itching all over your body, or any changes in your bowel habits such as blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and tight clothing suggest possible ascites or significant organ enlargement, which points toward advanced malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy.
